children: By Staff Writer
Air Tanzania on Friday reinstated its Moscow service less than 24 hours after suspending the route over security concerns arising from intensified Ukrainian airstrikes on Russia.
It reflected the difficult operating environment airlines face on flights to the Russian capital amid the ongoing conflict.
The Tanzanian carrier said a fresh risk assessment supported resumption of the three-times-weekly service from Dar es Salaam from Monday, September 7.
It launched its Moscow route on July 1, becoming the longest service on the Airline’s network and anchoring its long-haul expansion plans, after losing access to European Union airspace.
It was part of Tanzania’s efforts to strengthen air links with Russia and expand international connectivity.

But after two consecutive months of operating the thrice-weekly flights, Air Tanzania suspended them indefinitely after hostilities between Ukraine and Russia escalated, with Kyiv announcing increased drone activity over Moscow this week.

The carrier said the decision to suspend the route came after a “routine risk assessment”, which followed increased airstrikes on Russia by Ukraine as the conflict between the two countries dragged on.“The decision follows a routine risk assessment of the operating environment along the route. ATCL conducts these assessments continuously across our entire network, and where the outcome supports a pause, we take one. Safety considerations always take precedence over commercial ones,” the carrier said in a Thursday notice.

It was the first international carrier to suspend flights to Russia, even as Moscow said it would prevent any disruptions to air traffic in its airspace, while Kyiv warned that its drones were making it dangerous to fly into the country.

But as the airstrikes raged on, Air Tanzania announced a resumption of the service.“The resumption of services follows the completion of a routine operating environment risk assessment for the route, conducted in consultation with the relevant authorities,” it said in the Friday notice.
The flights are set to resume on Monday, September 7. It flies to Moscow every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
The brief suspension highlights the high risk of operating the route, which is one of the longest continuous flights, taking up to 11 hours to complete.
Having been banned from EU airspace due to safety risks by the bloc’s aviation regulator, Air Tanzania cannot fly over any EU country to Russia, forcing it to take the longer route via Asia.
Currently, it has to fly over Pakistan, Afghanistan and Turkmenistan, making the flight longer by several hours, but even this route has faced challenges due to increased tensions.
The other option is to fly over Iran, which is also currently in conflict and risky to fly over.
Air Tanzania said operational risk assessments are conducted continuously across its network and that services resume when the findings support continued operations.

The inaugural flight on the route landed at Moscow’s Vnukovo International Airport on July 2, carrying 123 passengers. Air Tanzania had planned to operate the Dar es Salaam–Moscow (Vnukovo)–Zanzibar service three times a week using its Boeing 787 Dreamliner.
The route has provided a direct link between Tanzania and Russia, serving tourists, business travellers and other passengers travelling between the two markets.
During the suspension, passengers booked on the affected flights were offered full refunds or changes to their travel dates or routes at no additional cost.
With the service now restored, passengers who postponed their journeys can reschedule without an additional charge by contacting Air Tanzania or their travel agents.

Those who had already received refunds will be required to make fresh bookings at fares applicable at the time of booking. Air Tanzania said it would continue monitoring conditions along the Moscow route and across its network and would take appropriate measures if the operating environment changes.
